title: Publish a product capability to Chancery
summary: Add or change a product-owned capability contract, stage it with the matching product release, and expose it through the installed directory without adding a runtime dependency.
use_when: A product gains or changes a user-facing capability or adaptive operation that should be globally discoverable.
An installed provider contract, manual, dependency, or selector must change.
do_not_use_when: Only product implementation changes while the published contract remains exact.
The proposed document is an unsupported aspiration, backlog item, brittle UI script, or internal primitive that users should not route to.
outcome: The owning product release contains a validated, version-matched bundle and owns one atomic installed provider selector that Chancery can read.
effects: Changes product-owned capability JSON, detailed manuals, packaging, and deployment tests.
A product deployment may atomically change that product's provider selector.
Does not change the product runtime's behavior or introduce a product-to-Chancery call.
authority: The product owns and reviews its supported outcomes, effects, commands, privacy, and recovery contract.
Chancery owns the bundle schema, validation rules, directory behavior, and cross-provider dependency presentation.
Global agent instructions own only the bootstrap that says when and how to query Chancery.
success: The source bundle passes chancery validate.
The product CI proves the bundle is staged and its provider selector follows current across install, update, and rollback.
After deployment, chancery doctor is valid and list/show expose the intended contract.
The product still runs when Chancery and its registry are absent.
failure_and_recovery: Reject the change before deployment if schema validation or product CI fails.
If deployment fails, restore the product release and provider selector together.
If one installed bundle later becomes invalid, leave other providers available and repair or redeploy only the owning product.
privacy: Contracts are installed local documentation and must not embed secrets, credentials, private source material, or transient runtime output.
A documented capability must separately state what its real invocation may retain or disclose.
does_not_authorize: Publishing a claimed capability that the product does not currently support.
Executing the represented capability or operation.
steps: Identify the durable user outcome and owning product before choosing an entry ID or mode.

Author a discriminative title and summary plus a self-contained manual from current product contracts, with semantic request boundaries, effects, authority, success, failure recovery, privacy, interfaces, and dependencies.
Validate the source bundle with the candidate Chancery reader before changing installed selectors.
Stage the unchanged bundle inside the owning product's content-addressed release and make its installer own exactly one registry selector.
Exercise product CI and deployment rollback, then deploy the product release.
Run Chancery doctor and confirm that list and show expose the installed contract with its full meaning and status.
checkpoints: The product owner confirms the capability describes supported current behavior rather than an aspiration.
Schema validation succeeds before installation state changes.
The staged bundle bytes and provider release metadata match the product release.
Installed discovery succeeds before any global bootstrap depends on the new entry.
adaptation: Use the product's own release layout and maintenance protocol; Chancery requires only a fixed bundle and atomic selector.
Describe volatile UI work semantically with checkpoints and stop conditions instead of selectors or coordinate scripts.
Split materially different outcomes or authority boundaries into separate entries so an agent can form a reliable semantic shortlist.
stop_when: The owning product does not yet support the claimed outcome.
The contract would need secret material or live state to be useful.
A dependency or authority owner cannot be identified.
The installer cannot update and roll back the product release and provider selector coherently.
